Match

Ice slides and takes a long time to stop. Mud grips badly and kills the roll.
Before the whistle: test your stick, stand on the side you want, and let bots fill the rest. Press Start to kick off. Cocktail always warms up so each seat can set which way is up. Controllers warms up only when a pad is connected; Everyone warms up on touch and keyboard too, with an on-screen Start. A controller can join a match already under way by pressing a button — see Joining late.
Plug a controller in during a match and a player walks out to the touchline. Walk up or down to the half you want, then press START — you come on at the next goal, on that side. The match grows to fit: a 3v3 that gains a player becomes a 4v4, with a bot added to the other side. Stand near the halfway line and you'll be put wherever Extra controllers says (opposite you for Versus, alongside for Co-op). Unplug and your body leaves by the same touchline gate, the sides even up again, and your goals stay on the scoresheet. At kickoff turns all of this off: seats are handed out once and a controller that wakes up mid-match waits for the next match.
Your side first (you, then your team-mates), then the opposition. Blank lines keep the default name. Applies to the next match.
Nobody crosses halfway until the ball is played — except inside the centre circle, which stays open so you can turn and pass back. Cross anywhere else and you're pushed home. Free-for-all once it's played.
One keeper and one attacker inside a goal box at a time — the net and the marked rectangle in front of it. Whoever gets there first holds the spot; anyone else gets half a second inside and is then eased back out, so you can run straight through without the pitch fighting you. Stops a team parking three bodies on their own line, and stops the attack burying the keeper under a scrum.
KICK stops being ball-only: a wall or a body in range takes the hit and you take the reaction. A wall has nothing to give, so kicking one launches you off it. Applies to everyone, bots included.

Game Feel

⚽ Ball controls
Trap lets you hold KICK to carry the ball, then release to shoot. One-touch kicks the instant you touch it — faster, much less forgiving. How long you can carry is the Trap window slider below.
🕹️ Player controls
Letting go of the movement stick shoots, so you can play with one thumb. The KICK button keeps working either way.
🎬 Presentation
Tilt the phone and the pitch and the players shift by slightly different amounts, so the pitch reads as something you're looking into rather than a flat picture. About ten pixels at full tilt — enough to feel, not enough to fight. Neutral is wherever you're actually holding the phone, so it works lying down. Render only: it never moves the ball or a player, only where they're drawn. Off automatically if your system asks for reduced motion.
A freeze-frame on the strike, but only when you first-touch a shot that's actually going in — the game checks the ball's path before it gives you one. Also fires on the goal itself. Set to 0 for none. Independent of screen shake.
On a goal the camera pushes in on whoever put it there. 1.0× is no push at all. Speed is how long the push takes, so a smaller number is a faster push. It always drifts back out slowly, whatever you set here. Both ride the Screen shake & effects toggle.
Ball and player speed plus your current feel numbers, bottom-left while you play.

Replays

A web page is never told where your browser puts downloads, so that is the usual place for this device rather than a path read off your disk — if your browser is set to ask each time, it is wherever you chose. Replays are saved from the Save replay button on the replay bar during a match, and from the result screen.

VJ Mode

Two video decks and two DJ decks, run from here while the game plays fullscreen on the projector. Everything is off until you turn it on, and the game looks and sounds exactly as normal until then.

The honest bit ❤

Magnetball is free, and everything that touches gameplay stays free — no pay-to-win, no ads, no loot boxes. The shop is cosmetics only: a way to support the game if you're enjoying it. You can also unlock every cosmetic just by playing and showing up for the daily reward. Coins buy nothing that helps you win — only how your disc looks.

How to Play

🎯 Goal. Push the ball into the opponent's net. Most goals before the clock runs out wins.

🕹️ Move. Touch and drag anywhere on the right half — a joystick appears under your thumb. Drag to steer; further = faster.

👟 Trap & shoot. Hold KICK and run into the ball. It sticks to your feet while you line up, then let go to shoot the way you're facing — hold longer for a harder strike (the ring round your disc fills as it charges). A quick tap instead of a hold is an instant pass. How long you can carry is the Trap window slider in Game Feel; set Ball control to One-touch there and the ball fires the moment you touch it, which is faster and far less forgiving.

🧊 Hit stop. First-touch a shot that's genuinely going in and the game freezes for a beat on the strike — it checks the ball's path before it gives you one, so a shot that goes wide, hits a body or dies short gets nothing. A trapped-and-carried shot doesn't count; this is for the first touch. Length is the Hit stop slider in Game Feel, and it's separate from Screen shake.

🧲 Magnet. Off by default — the ball is a free puck. Ball magnet (Game Feel, 0–100) adds a passive stick that carries the ball at your feet without holding KICK. Most people leave it at 0.

⏱ Kickoff. Both teams hold their own half until the ball is played. The centre circle is a gate: stand in it and you may cross the line early, so you can turn and pass backwards instead of only forwards. Stray over the line anywhere else and you're pushed back. Turn the whole rule off in the Match card.

🏆 Ranked. Matches against bots earn RP and climb the ladder (Wood → Legend); harder bots are worth more. Training is free practice with no clock. A timed game that's level at the whistle goes to sudden-death overtime — first goal wins.

🐌 Killer Queen. Two balls at once. The normal one scores as usual and re-serves from the centre, but nothing else resets — no kickoff, players hold position. The second is the snail: huge, heavy, and it can only be shoved, never kicked. Push it into their goal and the match ends there and then, whatever the score.

🧊 Surfaces. Grass grips. Ice slides and takes an age to stop. Mud grabs and kills the roll. Both wear in as you play — mud churns and ice picks up skate cuts where the traffic is.

👥 2-Player. Lay the phone flat between you. Player 1 uses the bottom controls, Player 2 the top (rotated) ones.

🎮 Controllers. Set Input to Controllers and connect gamepads (press a button to wake them). Each pad takes a seat — you first, then an opponent, then a teammate — so 2 pads is 1v1, 8 pads a full 4v4. Left stick moves, A / RT kicks. Empty seats stay bots. Extra controllers → Co-op fills your side first instead.

🤚 One hand. Game Feel → One-handed. Letting go of the movement stick shoots where you were heading, so you can play with one thumb. The KICK button still works.

⚙ Settings elsewhere. Display → Settings location → Separate tab moves every setting to /settings and leaves this page all game. Both stay in sync live, and that tab shows a running readout of ball and player speed.
